A formal sales process could begin as soon as 2026, per those same sources. Starbucks operates about 2,000 coffeehouses in Japan, which makes it one of the company's largest markets. The deliberations are ongoing and may not result in a sale, according to these people. A Starbucks spokesperson said the company continually assesses the best structure for its customers and creating value for shareholders, noting that the chain has maintained a strong business in Japan for more than 30 years. Citigroup and Morgan Stanley declined to comment.
items.title: Starbucks Engages Banks to Explore Sale of Japan Business

items.summary: At his first all-hands meeting since returning to lead the chipmaker he co-founded about three decades ago, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang rejected suggestions that President Donald Trump swayed the board to reinstate him. Speaking a day after the board brought him back following his earlier departure over revelations of extramarital relationships—one allegedly with a Chinese intelligence asset—Huang said the directors reviewed the facts and were assured his return posed no national security threat, according to The New York Times' live stream access. Nvidia stated its board was confident, after input from the US government, that reinstatement carried no national security risk; the move drew criticism from lawmakers of both parties who called for closer scrutiny. Trump has publicly claimed credit, telling CNBC in an interview he had spoken to the board and 'convinced them,' with reports indicating he reportedly pressured the board to rehire Huang. Addressing staff, Huang said he made serious mistakes and hurt his family and colleagues, quoting The New York Times as saying he was unfaithful to wife Lori and hurt his children; he admitted breaking the company's code of conduct was unacceptable and is in therapy, which he found helpful. He also pushed back on reports portraying him as an abusive boss and rejected that his position puts him above company rules. Nvidia and Huang face several state and federal probes or reviews by the FBI, Justice Department and SEC; Trump said November 9 that the FBI was 'looking into' the affair involving a Chinese businesswoman whom US intelligence agencies examined over whether she was a Chinese asset, while the board examines potential foreign intelligence activity, national security concerns and export controls. Huang agreed to testify at a public Senate Banking Committee hearing on December 3—chair Tim Scott said it will focus on oversight of US export controls—and he and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter confirmed they would appear for transcribed interviews with House committees on December 1 and 2. Trump told the New York Post that a pardon is 'always an option' but doesn't think it will be necessary, while also floating the possibility of the US government taking an equity stake in Nvidia.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Denies Trump's Influence In His Reinstatement, Will Testify Before US Senate

items.summary: At Nvidia's first all-hands meeting since his Monday reinstatement, founder Jensen Huang reportedly struck a remorseful tone, telling staff "I hurt all of you" and describing the gathering as one of the hardest meetings he has ever conducted. According to CNBC, Huang acknowledged that flouting Nvidia's code of conduct—which he had largely devised—was difficult for him personally, noting that his wife was present at an even harder meeting. As Wired reported his statement, Huang emphasized that violating a code of conduct does not automatically result in termination, citing mitigating circumstances. He stated that he is now in therapy and expressed gratitude for the second chance at the company. On Trump's role in his restoration, CNBC reports that President Trump reportedly called Nvidia's board directly to lobby for Huang's return; however, in his remarks, Huang downplayed this involvement. The Wall Street Journal reported that Huang thanked the administration on Tuesday for "providing Nvidia with quick access to intelligence" he said helped the board determine that national security risks from reinstating him were low. Looking ahead, CNBC notes that Huang will likely need continued administrative support as he faces congressional scrutiny under a newly Democrat-led government; he is scheduled to appear before the Senate Banking Committee next week and has been called for closed House hearings with the Intelligence Committee, Foreign Affairs Committee, and China Select Committee in coming weeks.
items.title: Jensen Huang Addresses Staff After Reinstatement, Cites Therapy and Thanks White House

items.summary:
The dollar slipped on Tuesday (Nov. 24), giving back much of Monday's gains, as a sharp rally in AI stocks sparked by Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO faded and traders questioned whether the greenback had climbed too far, too fast. The US currency has been supported by bets that the Federal Reserve will keep raising interest rates amid strong growth and inflation still above its 2 per cent target; Fed funds futures traders are pricing in 97 per cent odds of a December hike and a 66 per cent chance of an additional January increase, according to CME Group's FedWatch Tool. However, Elias Haddad, global head of markets strategy at Brown Brothers Harriman, said the US growth edge over the euro zone, UK, and Japan narrowed further in November, which could weigh on the dollar.

The dollar index fell 0.47 per cent to 103.81, with the euro up 0.6 per cent at $1.0966; the Japanese yen weakened 0.16 per cent against the greenback to 159.24 per dollar; sterling strengthened 0.64 per cent to $1.3112; and the Australian dollar gained 0.24 per cent to $0.6641, though it remained near 11-month lows after a drop of more than 5 per cent over the past month as traders price in rate cuts.

US data showed consumer confidence increased more than expected in November, touching its highest level in nearly two years amid optimism over labor market conditions and the economy following this month's midterm elections. German business morale also rose for a seventh straight month in November, boosting the single currency (euro).

Analysts at JPMorgan said short positions in the Australian dollar have accumulated substantially, with bearish positioning reaching extreme levels by their metrics; weekly data from US markets regulator shows speculators hold their largest bearish position in the Aussie on record, worth some $12.25 billion according to LSEG calculations. In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 2.40 per cent to $59,824.
items.title: Dollar Slips as Nvidia-Fueled AI Rally Fades

items.summary: Anthropic's stock fell below its $83 IPO price on Tuesday, trading as low as $76 a share by midday and dropping nearly 12% from Monday's close. Falling below the IPO price is often viewed negatively because underwriters typically price offerings at a discount to expected trading value. The slump comes less than a week after Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq at $111.50 per share, having opened above its initial public offering range of $83.
items.title: Anthropic Shares Fall Below IPO Price, a Worrying Sign for AI Startups

visual.alt: Bar chart. $111.50 IPO price 83 $; $76 low Tuesday close 76 $.

items.summary: The US is preparing to announce plans for new tariffs on several countries on Wednesday, according to the BBC. The proposed import taxes would affect many of America's biggest trading partners, with China, the European Union and Japan among at least 14 jurisdictions affected. This move follows the White House's Section 301 investigation, which was launched in March after the US Supreme Court ruled that President Donald Trump's Liberation Day tariffs were illegal.
items.title: US Preparing to Announce New Tariffs on at Least 14 Trading Partners

items.summary: The Indian rupee opened stronger at 92.74 against the US dollar, reflecting a 17 paise gain from the previous close amid market concerns about potential US tariffs on India and other nations. Domestic equities started December's derivative series positively, with the Nifty rising over 300 points driven by gains in private banks, financial services, and IT sectors. Commodities saw declines in gold and silver prices, while crude oil steadied near 90 dollars per barrel. Auto manufacturers announced December price hikes due to input costs despite relief from softer commodity prices.
items.title: Indian Rupee Strengthens Amid US Tariff Concerns as Equities Open Strong

items.summary: On Monday, Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, reversing a decision made just the previous week when the company told investors it had no intention of bringing him back. The reversal triggered a nearly $1 trillion surge in Nvidia's stock market valuation. Donald Trump took credit for the move, telling CNBC that he 'convinced them' to bring Huang back. Questions remain about Huang's extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy and whether Nvidia exploited loopholes to export chips to Chinese AI companies. Kai Wright spoke with Guardian US tech editor Blake Montgomery about the twists in the Huang scandal and why Huang embodies what they describe as the 'key man risk' that threatens our whole economy.
items.title: Nvidia Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, Sparking Nearly $1 Trillion Stock Surge

items.summary: The United States Trade Representative's Office is reportedly preparing duties on 16 economies over alleged industrial subsidies, with India among those potentially affected. According to reports by The Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg, the USTR may publish its findings in the coming days—Bloomberg reported tariffs could be announced as soon as Tuesday—but people familiar with the plans said timing remains subject to change. The White House and USTR have not responded publicly to the reports. India faces fresh US tariff risk as Trump weighs duties on 16 economies.
items.title: India Faces Fresh US Tariff Risk as Trump Weighs Duties on 16 Economies

items.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly preparing to increase tariffs on several countries, including China and India, arguing that their governments have harmed American companies by supporting domestic industrial production. Citing sources, The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday (local time) that Jamieson Greer, the US Trade Representative (USTR), may announce the tariffs as soon as this week. The move follows a months-long investigation into industrial subsidies provided by countries including China, the European Union, and 14 other nations.
items.title: US Preparing to Raise Tariffs on China, India and Others Under Section 301

items.summary: On Tuesday, November 24, 2026, the Federal Reserve Board released minutes from its meetings held on October 19 and October 28, 2026. The documents cover discussions of the discount rates provided to depository institutions through the discount window. According to a release dated for publication at 2:00 p.m. EST, the process used by the Board to set the discount rate is distinct from the process followed by the Federal Open Market Committee in setting its target range for the federal funds rate.
items.title: Federal Reserve Board Releases Minutes on October Discount Rate Meetings

items.summary: The administration of U.S. President Donald Trump is poised to imminently release the findings of a probe aimed at countering alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 major U.S. trading partners, according to three people with knowledge of the matter who spoke Tuesday. The investigation results are expected as soon as Tuesday afternoon, and new import duties on a wide range of goods are anticipated.
items.title: Washington to Unveil New Tariffs After Probe on Excess Factory Capacity

items.summary: Following Democrats' control of the House and Senate after the November 2026 midterms, a tracker maintained by Justin Hendrix and Dean Jackson (Nov. 24, 2026) documents what lawmakers have said they plan to investigate about technology companies once Congress convenes on January 3, 2027. The tracker collects statements in reverse chronological order from October through November 2026.
items.title: Democrats Map Tech Investigations Agenda Ahead of Jan. 3, 2027 Congress

items.summary: Three months after public disappointment following departures from Google DeepMind and underwhelming Gemini 3 models, the lab is being recast as an active frontier AI research effort. The outlet AINews — now part of Latent Space — dated its coverage to November 23–24, 2026, noting it checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters, and no further Discords when compiling the report.
items.title: Gemini 4 Neon Marks Google DeepMind's Return as a Frontier Lab

items.summary: The China Manned Space Agency announced on Wednesday that the launch of the crewed Shenzhou-24 spacecraft was successful. The Long March-2F Y24 carrier rocket lifted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China at 8:18 a.m. Beijing Time, and about 10 minutes later the spacecraft separated from the rocket and entered its preset orbit; the crew is reported to be in good condition. After entering orbit, the spacecraft will follow a planned procedure for an autonomous rapid rendezvous and docking with the space station complex before the Shenzhou-24 crew enters China's space station.
items.title: China Successfully Launches Shenzhou-24 Crewed Spacecraft

items.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday urged the party's 'PDA sentinels' across Uttar Pradesh to monitor the Election Commission's electoral roll activities ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. In a post on X, he asked workers to remain vigilant about changes to voter lists under two principles: "Not a single bogus vote to be added, not a single genuine vote to be removed!" Yadav also raised concerns over Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs), describing public scepticism with the phrase 'Haathi ke daant khaane ke aur, dikhaane keaur' ('All show, no substance'). He referenced what he called the BJP's 'Chandigarh trick,' noting people understood such political tactics. The Chandigarh mayoral election controversy centres on allegations of deliberate ballot tampering by presiding officer Anil Masih during the January 30, 2024, polls; the Supreme Court found Masih had deliberately marked eight ballots cast in favour of Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)-Congress candidate Kuldeep Kumar, leading to their wrongful rejection. The apex court quashed the initially declared result and declared Kumar the validly elected mayor of Chandigarh.
items.title: Akhilesh Yadav Urges SP Workers to Monitor Election Commission Ahead of 2027 UP Elections

items.summary: Around 300 members of the BJP and Hindu organisations have been booked over protests held Tuesday in Tamil Nadu's Thiruparankundram, according to news agency ANI citing Madurai Police on Wednesday. The cases were registered under six sections—unlawful assembly without permission, causing a breach of public peace, making controversial remarks, and obstructing government servants from discharging their duties—and relate to the non-lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon stone pillar atop the hill. Police attributed this failure to the state government's disregard for the Supreme Court's interim order directing that the lamp be lit there; instead, the Maha Deepam was lit above the Uchi Pillayar temple amid heavy security and rising tensions, while a small team of priests associated with the Subramaniya Swamy Temple performed the ceremony at 6:02 p.m., contrary to the court's directive for 6pm. Advocate and Hindu Munnani petitioner Niranjan S Kumar expressed disappointment over the decision, accusing the state government of deliberately disobeying the Supreme Court's interim order, and said further action would depend on a status report that Madurai District Collector was directed by the court to submit within three days of the festival. Tamil Nadu BJP leader Tamilisai Soundararajan also condemned the TVK government for violating the interim order, questioned why the lamp was lit at Uchi Pillayar temple citing Agama rules without prior disclosure, and alleged that BJP leaders and workers were prevented from approaching the temple while other political party leaders such as Thirumavalavan and Jawahirullah were allowed access. Protests over the issue were also reported elsewhere in Tamil Nadu: Hindu Front members staged a protest with a road blockade in Ramanathapuram after alleging failure to implement the Supreme Court's order, prompting police detention; and Hindu Munnani members staged a road blockade during the Maha Karthigai Deepam festival in Pollachi demanding government compliance with court directions before being removed by police amid brief tension. The protests came amid growing tensions over lighting the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon stone pillar, with Hindu organisations demanding that the state government comply with the Supreme Court's interim directions.
items.title: ~300 BJP and Hindu Group Members Booked Over Thiruparankundram Deepam Protests

items.summary:
The Trump administration is expected to soon announce plans to raise tariffs on India, China, the European Union, and 14 other economies, according to two people familiar with the matter who spoke anonymously. The US Trade Representative's Office is anticipated to release the results of a months-long tariff investigation into industrial subsidies by these 16 economies in the coming days, though officials stressed that timing for rollout could still change; neither the White House nor USTR responded to comment requests.

The planned tariffs are part of an effort to replace broader duties set last year — levies of 10 per cent to 12.5 per cent imposed on 60 trading partners in July over alleged inadequate enforcement of bans on forced-labour goods, and reciprocal tariffs struck down by the Supreme Court in February as unconstitutional. The new action constitutes a second step toward replacing those duties.

The White House frames the anticipated tariffs as a response to what it describes as excessive manufacturing output boosted by subsidies, which has led to lower-priced goods undercutting American companies. The investigation was initiated under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the president to levy tariffs against nations that discriminate against US commerce.

The specific levels of the new tariffs were not immediately clear but would come on top of existing duties of 10 per cent to 12.5 per cent announced earlier this year — rates many countries, including China, had protested and which took effect as temporary levies expired after the Supreme Court ruling. The expected move signals that the administration remains willing to impose import taxes despite a sweeping Republican loss in this month's midterm elections amid elevated inflation concerns.

The anticipated action also may test how Democrats respond to tariffs imposed unilaterally by Trump, who retains majorities in both chambers and could veto any legislation overturning or watering down the duties. The timing coincides with recent diplomatic engagement: Trump visited Shenzhen last week for his third face-to-face meeting this year with Chinese President Xi Jinping, who is expected to travel to Doral, Florida, next month for the G20 Summit that Trump is hosting.

The trade friction centers on China's massive industrial capacity across autos, solar panels, cement and steel manufacturing. Although Chinese leaders have prioritized rebalancing the economy, slowing domestic demand has prompted companies to expand into overseas markets, pushing China's trade surplus to a record of nearly USD 1.2 trillion last year.
items.title: US Plans Fresh Tariffs on India, China and 14 Other Countries

items.summary: According to Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) data, active mutual funds captured 81% of new fund offerings inflows during the April–October 2026 period. Fund houses launched 51 actively managed schemes that raised ₹14,200 crore between April and October 2026, compared with ₹3,200 crore mobilised by 87 passive schemes over the same period. A Balasubramanian, MD and CEO of Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC, said active funds have beaten their benchmark indices and outperformed passive schemes despite stock market volatility in the past two years. Vikas Khemani, founder and chairman of Carnelian Asset Management, attributed strong inflows into actively managed funds to scope for generating alpha in India, noting that a 2-3% outperformance makes it worthwhile given comparable cost structures between active and passive funds.
items.title: Active Mutual Funds Attract Majority of FY27 NFO Inflows in India

items.summary: The reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia's boss has intensified divisions within the Trump administration and provided a political issue for both Republican and Democratic presidential candidates ahead of the 2028 election. According to Semafor's politics team, Vice President JD Vance played a role in Huang's return, creating contrast with Secretary of State Marco Rubio's more hawkish stance; both men are viewed as contenders for the Republican nomination. Potential Democratic nominees have also leveraged the situation by decrying alleged corruption at the center of Huang's reinstatement, with leading governors and senators raising concerns. Both Nvidia's chief executive and the U.S. commerce secretary—who is accused of a lax attitude toward enforcement of chip controls—are scheduled to testify before Congress soon.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia Reinstatement Shakes Washington

items.summary: Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's chief executive is being framed by observers as a political victory for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who has faced pressure from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and others to tighten restrictions on chip exports to China. According to the reporting, Lutnick declined to blacklist Megaspeed—an Nvidia customer—despite months of entreaties, while President Trump reportedly agreed with his inaction by asserting that acting could provoke a confrontation with China. The White House pointed to Bessent's Sunday remarks characterizing Huang as now being 'on the outside,' and Bessent separately adopted a softer stance on Sunday, stating that Nvidia's culture outweighed 'one person's foibles.' That same day, Nvidia announced Huang's return, citing administration officials' assurances that his reinstatement 'poses no national security risk'; the announcement reportedly sent AI stocks soaring. The report attributes to a White House source claims that Lutnick avoided being fired earlier this year through a $25 million donation to Trump's presidential library, and a White House official dismissed as 'baseless and wildly reckless speculation' any suggestion that Lutnick's position depends on such a contribution, asserting instead that Trump has maintained complete confidence in the secretary. The Treasury and Commerce Departments did not comment.
items.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO Amid Cabinet Tensions

items.summary: Reporting from the Financial Times indicates that Tesla and SpaceX have appointed five directors—three from Tesla's board (Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson, and Jack Hartung) and two from SpaceX's board (Roelof Botha and Randy Glein)—to explore a potential merger. Reuters reported separately that Elon Musk stated on SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call last month that unifying his AI, robotics, EV, and aerospace ambitions under one corporate roof would be 'a good idea,' and confirmed the companies had formed special committees of independent directors to discuss the union. The expectation for such a merger has existed since at least SpaceX's IPO, though it was previously based more on speculation about Musk's preferences than concrete evidence; a merger would give him greater control over the combined company. The article raises national security concerns, noting Tesla's heavy dependence on China for sales and production while SpaceX is a key military supplier, which could expose the merged entity to Chinese pressure.
items.title: Tesla and SpaceX Form Joint Director Committees to Explore Merger

items.summary: Earlier this year the United States made a preliminary determination that Mexico had been dumping winter strawberries into the country at uncompetitively low prices. That ruling triggered new tariffs of up to 5.25% on the fruits, with a final determination expected early next year. Approximately 5,000 Mexican strawberry growers are impacted by the measure.
items.title: Mexico's strawberry growers face US tariffs amid dumping claims

items.summary: Natalia Viana argues that Brazil's recent elections demonstrated how societies can resist Big Tech and its alliance with anti-democratic forces, presenting a model for other countries. The article frames this as a historic moment following Brazil's January 8, 2023 attempted coup led by former president Jair Bolsonaro, which the country prosecuted and punished — dozens of military personnel are now in prison while Bolsonaro remains under house arrest.
items.title: Brazil's Elections Offer Hope in the Fight Against Big Tech

items.summary: The Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) responded in a letter signed by Senior Vice-President Lynn Lee to Ives Tay's Nov 18 letter titled 'How are lean MNCs here benefiting Singaporeans' employment prospects?' The EDB argued that while individual multinational corporation headquarters may operate with lean teams, they collectively create good jobs and career pathways for Singaporeans across functions including marketing, finance, supply chain management, technology, and legal services. According to the EDB, among MNCs with HQ functions supported by it, about 70% of employees are locals, and more than two-thirds of these local employees earn over $6,000 a month. The letter stated that having regional and global decision-making functions based in Singapore gives workers exposure to international markets, business leaders, and specialist expertise while creating pathways to senior roles. It also noted EDB initiatives such as the Singapore Leaders Network Fellowship and Global Business Leaders Programme designed to develop Singaporeans for leadership positions, and encouraged taking on overseas assignments to build commercial experience needed for senior HQ roles overseeing multiple markets.
items.title: Singapore Economic Development Board Responds to Claims About MNC Headquarters Employment

items.summary: According to a report from Monday, U.S. President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance personally intervened in Nvidia's decision over the weekend to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang, who had resigned earlier that month amid reports of extramarital affairs including one with an alleged Chinese spy. People familiar with the matter told Reuters that both officials were convinced Huang alone protected American-made open-weight AI models—systems whose core components are publicly available for users to download, modify and adapt—and that his growth represents a major business opportunity because it broadens demand for Nvidia's chips beyond large developers. The report notes China leads in developing these systems, which US companies find cheaper than proprietary tools from OpenAI and Anthropic while performing nearly as well. Reuters reported separately on November 18 that the Trump administration was considering requiring U.S. companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models, including open-weight ones, to reduce reliance on Chinese technology. Nvidia has been a prominent backer of the ecosystem: it agreed in August to buy Hugging Face and is an investor in Reflection AI, which launched its first open-weight model in October. Huang's lobbyists have also pressed lawmakers against what he called
items.title: Trump and Vance Intervened in Nvidia's Decision to Reinstate Jensen Huang

items.summary: Kilmar Ábrego García is leaving the United States for Spain, taking a commercial flight to the country on Tuesday according to CBS News. His departure follows years of legal battles over his deportation after he was wrongfully sent back to El Salvador in March 2025 and held in Cecot prison under harsh conditions. After the government admitted it had deported him in error, Ábrego García returned to the US where human trafficking charges against him were dismissed by a federal judge who said he had been charged for political reasons. The administration then continued attempts to deport him to other countries including Uganda, Ghana, and Liberia before Costa Rica agreed to accept him as a refugee with legal status. His deportation case became a flashpoint in debate over President Donald Trump's immigration agenda. Senator Chris Van Hollen visited Ábrego García while he was imprisoned in El Salvador in 2025 and advocated for his release, stating that the Trump Administration had wanted to leave him "to rot in a Salvadoran gulag" before describing him now as traveling to a country of his choice as a free man. His lawyer said the departure is temporary because he has many options to return to the United States, expecting the next administration will prioritize reunifying his family and bringing him back to Maryland where he lived with his US citizen wife.
items.title: Kilmar Ábrego García Leaving US for Spain After Deportation Battle

items.summary: About 100 football clubs, representing hundreds of thousands of players, have deliberately missed the deadline to sign up for next season in a dispute with Football Queensland. Representatives of 110 clubs — about half of Queensland's football clubs — attended a Tuesday night meeting a day before the governing body's registration deadline and unanimously agreed not to register. The group includes nine of the 12 men's National Premier League clubs and six of the nine women's National Premier League clubs, according to figures cited in reporting on the dispute.
items.title: Breakaway group of 110 Queensland football clubs deliberately misses registration deadline amid revolt over fees

items.summary: President Abelardo de la Espriella arrived by motorcade in the tourist city of Cartagena on Tuesday night to take control of an operation involving scores of officers, navy personnel, and special forces responding to a hostage siege. The standoff involved gunmen holding at least 20 people inside an Éxito supermarket in the La Castellana neighbourhood, located about six miles from the old city's fortress walls overlooking the Caribbean. About 30 people were initially seized early Tuesday morning, but by nightfall police said 10 hostages — five of them elderly women — had been released, with no reported injuries so far.
items.title: Colombia's President Arrives at Supermarket Hostage Siege in Cartagena

items.summary: Azfar Mustaqim Jasman, a 26-year-old former auxiliary police officer with Certis CISCO who held the rank of sergeant, was jailed for eight weeks on Wednesday (Nov 25) after negligently raising an anti-terrorism vehicle barrier that struck a public bus at Changi Airport Terminal 3. The incident occurred on May 21, 2024, at about 12.45pm when the driver of Tower Transit bus service 858 was transporting at least 23 passengers from Woodlands Interchange to Changi Airport Terminal 3. After the bus passed through a raised drop-arm barrier for security checks and proceeded toward the Terminal 3 basement, Jasman—who had lowered the anti-terrorism vehicle barrier earlier to allow a light goods vehicle into the basement but failed to raise it afterward—negligently leaned forward with his left hand on the control panel while looking at the passing bus rather than the equipment. This depressed a button that raised the barrier and caused the collision; the prosecution stated there were no known faults and the barrier was in good working condition, and Jasman had been trained to operate it and knew he was prohibited from leaning casually on the control panel per internal standard operating procedures. The crash injured 22 people including the driver (whose name was redacted), who suffered a nasal bone fracture with seven days of hospitalisation leave, while another 20 victims sustained bruises, lacerations and other injuries; Jasman pleaded guilty to causing grievous hurt through a negligent act toward the driver, with a second charge for hurting passengers taken into consideration. The damaged barrier cost S$55,335 (US$42,884) to repair at Changi Airport Group's expense, and the bus was scrapped as a total loss valued at S$236,515.57; the prosecution sought seven to 10 weeks in jail, noting that although the driver's injury was serious it was not permanent or surgically significant, but emphasizing that Jasman had been entrusted to protect Singapore's critical national infrastructure and breached clear procedures without justification. His lawyer Elliot Teng of Regal Law requested a fine of S$5,000 or alternatively no more than two weeks in jail, arguing his client was relatively new (having served about nine months as an auxiliary police officer) but had cooperated fully with investigators, helped the victims by informing superiors, reflected on and apologized to each victim.
items.title: Ex-auxiliary police officer jailed after raising anti-terrorism barrier, causing bus crash at Changi Airport

items.summary: Workers' unions representing about 10,000 workers at the Indonesia Morowali Industrial Park (IMIP), the world's largest nickel-smelting complex, are resisting a new collective bargaining agreement because employers refused to let them participate in workplace health and safety committees that file formal incident reports. The dispute follows deadly accidents, including a December 2023 furnace blast owned by Tsingshan subsidiary Indonesia Tsingshan Stainless Steel that killed 21 workers, after which the unions launched a five-day sit-in at government labor department offices in Morowali district, Central Sulawesi province; they called off the sit-in on Nov. 7 this year as employers moved to file and bring into force an agreement workers had not signed. Workers have been without a new collective agreement since 2023, after talks collapsed when union members said employers failed to attend crucial discussions over health and safety committee membership.
items.title: Unions reject collective bargaining agreement at Indonesia's largest nickel hub amid deadly accidents

items.summary: On Wednesday, China launched its Shenzhou-24 space mission carrying three astronauts toward the Tiangong space station. The launch marked a milestone as astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became the first foreign national to board the Tiangong space station. According to the report, the mission is expected to last several days before he returns to Earth.
items.title: China Launches Shenzhou-24 Mission With First Pakistani Astronaut Aboard

items.summary: Australia signed a new treaty with the Solomon Islands on Wednesday in Canberra aimed at rolling back China's access to the Pacific and partly reversing Beijing's gains from a 2022 deal that offered China security access to the island nation just before Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese took office. The agreement is described as the culmination of Albanese's efforts to counter that earlier arrangement, which had alarmed the United States and its allies three years ago. Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale said in a joint appearance with Albanese that the archipelago 'has been for a number of years a source of uncertainty and doubt in the region,' adding without specifically mentioning the China deal that 'those days are done.'
items.title: Australia Signs Treaty With Solomon Islands to Counter China

items.summary:
Music streaming service Tidal announced on Tuesday that it will ban entirely AI-generated music from its platform, with the policy taking effect on December 9. The company stated that tracks made solely using AI tools would be rejected if their metadata reveals they were generated exclusively by AI, while songs created with AI assistance remain permitted. Tidal said AI music “diverts streams and royalties away from the artists, and confuses fans.”

The Norwegian-US streaming service reported a significant increase in fully AI-generated content over recent months. In the past 90 days, it identified 43% of distributed tracks as 100% AI-generated, with 27 million songs on its platform — representing 6.3% — tagged as entirely AI. On November 6 alone, Tidal said 60% of uploaded songs were 100% AI-generated.

Tidal reported that subscribers are not listening to these tracks: 96% have received zero streams in the last three months. The company added it had taken down 65,000 tracks flagged as suspected impersonations of real artists, describing wholly AI music intended to mislead listeners and impersonate artists as “another serious problem that has only increased in scale.” Tidal said its policy is the most stridently against AI among all major streaming services.

Bandcamp announced a ban on music generated wholly or in substantial part by AI in January. Spotify and Apple Music label AI tracks and artists but still allow fully generated songs to be distributed; Spotify has promised users tools for making AI-generated remixes and cover songs, while also removing about 50 million “slop” tracks from recommendations and deleting 75 million “spammy” tracks in October.
items.title: Tidal Bans Fully AI-Generated Music and Plans to Delete Millions of Tracks

items.summary: According to a Bloomberg News report on Tuesday, Starbucks has engaged advisers and banks including Citigroup and Morgan Stanley to prepare for the potential sale of its Japan business in a deal worth several billion dollars. The report cites people familiar with the matter as it states that Starbucks has begun sounding out interest from some strategic and financial investors. Reuters was unable to immediately verify the report. This follows earlier reporting by Reuters in September, which indicated that Starbucks was weighing the sale of a majority stake in its Japan business in a potential deal that could value the coffee chain's largest overseas company-operated market at about $3 billion.

items.summary: North Korea has ordered Switzerland to close its newly opened diplomatic office in Pyongyang and given the mission's head, Astier Sylvain, 48 hours to leave the country as persona non grata. The move comes after Bern added North Korea's Songdowon International Children's Camp near Wonsan to its sanctions list over Russia's war in Ukraine, citing that the facility exposes Ukrainian children from Russian-occupied territory to pro-Russian propaganda. State news agency KCNA reported Wednesday that a senior Foreign Ministry official handed Sylvain a written demand for closure following Tuesday's warning from Kim Yo Jong, who called the sanctions an 'open hostile act' violating North Korean sovereignty and defended the camp as serving 'legitimate' cooperation between Pyongyang and Moscow. The expulsion occurs five weeks after Switzerland reopened its office on 19 October when Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis visited Pyongyang to meet officials including Choe Son Hui; KCNA said the talks covered promoting dialogue and cooperation, with the office reporting to Bern's embassy in Beijing.
items.title: North Korea Expels Swiss Diplomat Over Sanctions on Children's Camp

items.summary: A close friend of Noemi Kondacs, who is facing a Supreme Court murder trial in Brisbane over the death of her seven-month-old son Rhuan Bosch in November 2022, told the jury this week that she had concerns about the child's welfare in the months before he died. The 26-year-old Kondacs is representing herself and entered not guilty pleas on both counts of murder and failure to provide the necessaries of life; Justice Paul Smith entered those pleas after she declined to plead earlier in the trial. Crown prosecutor Elise Adams called Christine Potgieter, a friend of Kondacs and her husband Reinhardt Bosch through church, who testified that while the couple had seemed happy before Rhuan's birth, she began worrying about his welfare from their first meeting over details such as all of his blankets being dirty with no washing machine and uncertainty whether he had a cot. On the final visit in the month before his death, Potgieter said she was alarmed by Rhuan's low weight and inability to focus his eyes; when she raised her concerns about his weight, Kondacs assured her that he had been seen by doctors only two weeks earlier and all was fine. The jury has already heard medical evidence will be presented showing Rhuan allegedly weighed less than two kilograms more than his birth weight at the time of his death, dropping from the 67th percentile to beneath the 3rd percentile for children his age. Potgieter also testified that Kondacs had expressed concerns during pregnancy about their financial preparedness and ability to support themselves, noting she took shopping for maternity clothes after Kondacs said she was wearing her husband's underpants as it was all she found comfortable; although Potgieter offered to pay for scans and help with money, the couple refused further assistance. During visits once Rhuan was born, Potgieter said Kondacs would only change his nappy in the car and never saw him naked at her home, while Bosch wanted him to nap in his car seat with windows down; when Potgieter heard the baby crying loudly outside one day and told the parents, Bosch pushed Kondacs down before returning inside. She described Bosch as strong-willed and manipulative for isolating Kondacs by stopping her from working and selling her car, and said he made comments about having a submissive wife and needing to discipline his child. The trial continues.
items.title: Friend of mother accused of murder tells Brisbane jury she worried about baby's health

In the latter half of the 19th century, a literary revival in Telugu—strongly influenced by Sanskrit and English literature—took place within the British-administered Madras Presidency. The National Library in Kolkata recorded that among 670 total records of Shakespeare translations and adaptations done across Indian languages up to 1964, 128 were in Bengali, 97 in Marathi, 83 in Tamil, 70 in Hindi, 66 in Kannada, and 62 in Telugu. These Telugu translations produced a corpus of prose and dramatic texts showing that Shakespeare’s plays had become part of the region’s cultural scenario rather than only studied works.

Telugu was spoken across parts of present-day Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Odisha, and Telangana within the Madras Presidency. The 1871 census recorded 11,610,000 Telugu speakers in the presidency, rising to 14,276,509 by the 1901 census; at India’s independence in 1947, Tamil and Telugu speakers together comprised over 78% of the presidency’s population. Before Shakespeare arrived, theatrical performances chiefly consisted of Kuchipudi dance dramas based on the puranas and folk forms such as burrakatha and tholibomma aata.

The arrival of touring Parsi theatre companies from Bombay in the latter part of the 19th century prompted local people to form drama companies, leading to Telugu-language productions. The Dharwar School troupe from Maharashtra similarly influenced Telugu theatre; these groups staged plays based on Kalidasa and Shakespeare and helped develop local companies such as Surabhi Theatre.

Several translators produced notable works in this period. Vavilala Vasudeva Sastri (1851–1897) translated Julius Caesar in 1876, retaining character names while adding the common Telugu suffix “-udu” and rendering it in verse modeled on iambic pentameter. Gurazada Sriramamurti (1851–1899), a scholar at the court of King Ananda Gajapathiraju of Vizianagaram, translated The Merchant of Venice as Venusu Vanija Naatakamu in 1880 using both prose and verse. CSR Krishnamma produced an 1895 Telugu prose translation of Macbeth.

Kandukuri Veeresalingam (1848–1919), called the father of modern Telugu literature, began a Telugu drama association in the Madras Presidency in 1880 and staged his own play Vyavahara Dharma Bodhini along with his translation of Shakespeare’s Comedy of Errors as Chamatkara Ratnavali on April 16, 1880. He also translated The Merchant of Venice from Charles and Mary Lamb’s Tales from Shakespeare (printed at Vivekavarthani Press in Rajahmundry in 1880), changing character names to fit the Telugu ethos.

Missionary activity had earlier built churches and Anglo-vernacular schools, including the first such school established by Samuel Dey’s Telugu Baptist Church in Nellore in 1840. The Godavari Delta Mission set up its headquarters at Narsapur after Sir Arthur Cotton brought missionaries back from England in 1836; it founded an Anglo-Telugu school in 1844 and a printing press at Visakhapatnam that printed religious books in Telugu.

Veeresalingam, also known as Veerasalingam Pantalu and a social reformer advocating women’s education, widow remarriage, and the abolition of child marriage, believed English education would rejuvenate Telugu culture. In 1875 he wrote that western lore had refined native manners and dispelled superstition, arguing translation into Telugu was necessary to make such texts available without access to English education.

He is credited with modernizing Telugu literary language by shifting it from classical style toward colloquial forms, increasing prose use in essays, biographies, autobiographies, and novels. The material derives from “Shakespeare in Telugu in the Nineteenth Century” by Nishi Pulugurtha in Travelling Texts: Translating Nineteenth-Century European Classics into Indian Languages, edited by Shantanu Majee and K Subramanyam (Routledge).
items.title: Telugu Shakespeare Translations Reshaped 19th-Century Madras Presidency Culture

Retail inflation in India climbed to 6.09% in October, up from 5.54% in September, with food prices surging to 8.94%. The squeeze was sharper in rural areas (9.09%) than urban ones (8.68%), as food prices rose considerably faster than the overall inflation rate.

Economists attribute this year's food inflation to weather disruptions, supply shortages and rising input costs. India remains acutely vulnerable to monsoon variability since nearly 60% of its farmland depends on rainfall; this year's southwest monsoon was 13% below normal while intensifying El Niño conditions raised risks to farm production.

Food accounts for a smaller share of household spending than before but still drives inflation, representing 36.75% of the consumer price index basket—down sharply from 45.86% under the previous series as Indians spend more on services and non-food items.

The impact is uneven across income groups: according to Dharmakirti Joshi at Crisil, the bottom 20% of rural households faced inflation of 6.9% in October versus 6.5% for the richest 20%, while urban rates were 6.1% and 5.3%. Rajeswari Sengupta noted that adjustability is lower in poorer countries because a larger share of household income goes to food.

The pressure shows up even in meal costs: Crisil's Roti Rice Rate analysis found the cost of a home-cooked vegetarian thali rose 12% year-on-year, with rice up about 10%, pulses 8%, edible oil 13% and LPG 10%. Pushan Sharma said prices are becoming broad-based rather than driven by just a few commodities.

Perishables like onions and tomatoes cause sudden spikes due to seasonal swings and storage weaknesses. The rabi onion crop, accounting for roughly two-thirds of production, is harvested in March-April and stored for months; tomatoes spike during summer when arrivals decline or heat stress affects output. Sharma said perishables drive volatility while staples structurally increase costs over time.

Economists say India lacks adequate infrastructure to sort, grade, store and process much of its perishable produce, though better storage could convert surplus into products like puree. Other pressures include energy shocks affecting transport and inputs, rising fertiliser prices, and reliance on imported edible oil.

Government stocks offer some protection: cereal reserves are above minimum levels and the free-food programme covers nearly 800 million people, with rice stocks particularly ample. Sengupta warned of a wider risk—a wage-price spiral where workers demand higher pay to cover living costs, pushing businesses to raise prices further.

The government faces a balancing act between protecting farmers through minimum support prices and managing politically sensitive food prices via measures like export restrictions or stockpile limits. A consumption survey analysis showed cereals' share of food spending has fallen sharply among the poorest households while dairy, fruit and meat consumption increased across income groups.
items.title: India's Food Inflation Surges to 8.94% as Overall Retail Prices Rise

Jury member Carol Guzy, a Pulitzer Prize-winning photojournalist, and winner Giles Clarke spoke to Anadolu on Tuesday during a reception at the İstanbul Photo Awards 2026 exhibition in Washington, DC. The two said photojournalism plays a key role in raising awareness of global crises.

Guzy praised the contest's entries as powerful work documenting the world, saying photographers provide 'such a service for humanity.' She added that photographs can open people's eyes and shake them out of complacency, hoping they make viewers feel and perhaps act. On the judging process, Guzy said there were too many good pictures to choose from, with so much powerful and heart-wrenching work that 'we couldn't give enough awards,' describing some as images that sear themselves into memory.

Photojournalist Giles Clarke won third prize in the Daily Life single category for his photograph "Born By Phone Light," taken in eastern Sudan. He said it was a real honor to receive the award, especially given work from Sudan, which he has covered over the last two years and which needs more coverage. The photograph shows a newborn baby lying on a hospital bed beside her mother.

Clarke took the image in March 2025 after a drone struck a nearby hydroelectric plant and cut power to the area. With no diesel for generators, doctors had little to work with; he saw a mother and baby tended by phone lights and was told the baby had been born by phone light. He described it as typical of what is happening in Sudan today.

Clarke praised the contest for not shying away from difficult subjects, noting colleagues are doing incredible work worldwide 'from Gaza to Ukraine,' though he said it is really hard to get into places and tell those stories.

The exhibition runs at the 11:Eleven Gallery in the National Press Building through Dec. 5. It features more than 90 photographs by the 25 winners of the contest's 12th edition, covering famine in Gaza caused by Israeli attacks and a blockade, wildfires in California, struggles of Afghan children, life being rebuilt in post-war Syria, space debris, portraits of Ukraine's cultural heritage, and daily life in Kenya.

Turkcell is this year's communications sponsor, the Turkish Cooperation and Coordination Agency (TIKA) supports overseas events, and Turkish Airlines provides airline sponsorship.
items.title: İstanbul Photo Awards Jury Member and Winner Highlight Photojournalism's Role in Raising Awareness of Global Crises

Zama Khan said the party is confident under Nishant Kumar, who would draw inspiration from and carry forward his father's legacy; Shyam Rajak called him a proven administrator with mass support and youth appeal, saying 'Nitish is our leader and our future leader is Nishant'; BJP state spokesperson Prem Ranjan Patel said Nishant has the same agility, conviction and patience as his father and that promoting him would strengthen the party. As the UN's annual 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence begins November 25 and runs until December 10, International Human Rights Day, experts are urging that activism demand concrete action against online perpetrators rather than relying on symbolic declarations. The campaign is supported by the UN Secretary-General's UNiTE to End Violence Against Women initiative with this year's call for justice, protection of survivors, and ending impunity.

The article argues that technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV) has become a formidable delivery mechanism for misogyny, communal prejudice, and social control. Investigative journalist Rana Ayyub describes her 2018 experience as the target of a coordinated digital assault: after reporting in 2018 challenged powerful interests, a pornographic video featuring her morphed face was circulated widely alongside doxxing of her personal information. She reported that the fan page of a Bharatiya Janata Party leader shared the video, which it then distributed an additional 40,000 times before reaching nearly every phone in India.

Cyber-safety expert Gautam Mengle explains that creating a convincing sexual deepfake now requires no specialized knowledge or expensive software. He states that "it takes a few minutes and no skill," noting that a single clear photo from an Instagram profile or WhatsApp display picture is sufficient, with free apps and Telegram bots completing the process. He adds that output quality has crossed the point where casual viewers cannot distinguish real content, emphasizing that in this crime the casual viewer—such as a friend, family member, or colleague—is enough.

Mengle warns that the nightmare begins when material circulates: a video uploaded on one platform can quickly spread to Telegram groups, adult websites, mirror sites, and private messaging networks. He explains that "every copy is a fresh upload," so removing the original does not eliminate copies elsewhere. This dynamic means technology manufactures sexual abuse faster than response systems can act.

Actor Rashmika Mandanna's November 2023 experience brought these dangers into national conversation when a viral elevator video was manipulated to replace her face with that of a British-Indian woman; the main accused was arrested in January 2024. Mandanna emphasized the vulnerability of women lacking celebrity status or public platforms, asking what would happen if such an image were shared among ordinary college students and their parents.

Influencer Archita Phukan's case illustrates monetization of fabricated sexual identities: her ex-boyfriend allegedly used a photograph to create an AI-generated online persona that reportedly attracted over 1.4 million followers and generated adult-content revenue, with rumors spreading she had joined the American pornography industry. Investigating officer Sizal Agarwal described how harassment "soon turned into a profit-making business," noting the technology constructed an alternative sexual identity for commercial consumption.

Experts stress that violence cannot be understood through gender alone but is shaped by intersecting identities including caste, religion, class, disability, and sexual identity. Dalit rights activist Ganpat Bhise explains that caste prejudice can make justice struggles harder when survivors approach police or courts, citing a case of a Dalit sex worker pressured to strip on video call who faced mockery from both client and police.

Women's Studies expert Dr Tejaswini Sevekari points out that Muslim women confront patriarchy alongside Islamophobia. She cites the Sulli Deals (2021) and Bulli Bai (2022) applications, which scraped hundreds of publicly available photographs of Muslim women for mock auctions designed to sexualize an entire community. Former journalist Hiba Beg described being "sold online" while censoring herself from public speech.

Trans rights activist Grace Gulati warns that technology reproduces and intensifies existing inequalities in the digital world rather than erasing them, affecting disabled women, refugees, migrants, trans women, and informal labor workers through compounded risks of trafficking with limited legal protection access.

The most insidious consequence may be self-censorship. Law graduate Geetha Hariprasad replaced her social media profile photo with an illustration fearing AI-powered nudification misuse. Mengle argues the biggest vulnerability lies in society's response to survivors, noting that women are routinely advised to stay indoors, plead with perpetrators, or avoid attention while facing blame for trusting wrong people.

Sevekari explains this becomes digital abuse as a tool of social control: "The perpetrators do not need to silence every woman. They only need to make enough women afraid." Survivors may stop expressing political opinions, withdraw from professional networks, or disappear entirely.

Institutional responses compound trauma through police unfamiliar with deepfake technology, reluctance to register complaints, investigation delays, and difficult grievance mechanisms. Equality Now research on TFGBV in India documents institutional friction including apathy, victim-blaming, and difficulties accessing legal remedies. The transnational nature of digital abuse worsens the problem as perpetrators operate anonymously using platforms hosted outside India.

Sameer P, project lead of Meri Trustline at Rati Foundation supporting survivors across more than 26 Indian states, describes content reappearing on other platforms after removal. His organization's report "Make It Real: Mapping AI-Facilitated Gendered Harm" highlights how abuse multiplies rapidly and repeatedly resurfaces while calling for greater platform transparency.

India's regulatory framework is beginning to address these dangers through the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026 notified in February. These rules bring synthetically generated information within regulation, strengthen intermediary due-diligence obligations, introduce identification and labeling requirements for permissible synthetic content, add measures preventing unlawful AI-generated material, and reduce grievance redressal timelines to two hours for sensitive complaints involving nudity and impersonation. Existing Information Technology Act and Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita provisions may also apply depending on offense nature.

Sevekari argues strengthening institutions is as important as laws, calling for police, healthcare workers, and judicial authorities trained to handle cases sensitively with survivor-centered responses recognizing barriers faced by marginalized women. She stresses better data needs beyond case numbers to understand how caste, religion, disability, and other factors shape experiences so no group is overlooked.

Mengle advises survivors preserving evidence before removal attempts: screenshots capturing complete webpage, URL, username, date and time; screen recordings of posts, profiles, comments; copies of links and threatening messages saved securely with trusted help. He directs complaints to the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) or calling 1930 while cautioning against deleting evidence in panic, paying blackmailers, engaging perpetrators directly, or forwarding material indiscriminately.

Mengle emphasizes responsibility cannot end with precautionary checklists for women; "every household must create a culture where a victim can speak up without being afraid." Sevekari insists the campaign must translate into accountable platforms, responsive policing, accessible legal remedies, survivor-centered services, and sustained prevention investment while challenging cultures making women responsible for preventing violence.

She concludes that if women must choose between public voice and personal dignity "something has gone profoundly wrong," questioning why perpetrators feel emboldened, platforms remain difficult to hold accountable, and survivors defend their own dignity. Until fear shifts from survivor to perpetrator there will be no meaningful safe mode online.

In Ayyub's case she submitted at least 200 screenshots and links identifying accounts through which material circulated; police reportedly stopped searching for culprits in 2020 claiming perpetrators could not be identified.
items.title: Activism Against Gender-Based Violence Urges Action on Online Perpetrators

Excerpts from a newly published compilation titled 'The Private Diary of Pope Francis,' compiled by Cardinal Victor Manuel Fernandez, head of the Vatican's Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, were released Tuesday (25 November 2026). The book contains excerpts from the late pontiff's diary, notes, and documents dating from 1992 to 2024. According to Cardinal Fernandez, who said Pope Francis—who died in April 2025—asked him to make his personal writings known to the world, the publication reveals spiritual experiences, fears over clerical sexual abuse, and discussions on allowing married men to become priests.

The book does not contain the complete diary. Its excerpts are accompanied by comments from Fernandez, who said Francis recorded his most confidential thoughts in an indecipherable code that is not included in the publication. The work has been published in five languages across 94 countries.

In a passage written in January 2021, Pope Francis described experiencing 'spiritual visions,' including encounters with the devil. According to the notes, he experienced three such visions during his life. He said the first occurred when he was a bishop in Buenos Aires: "I saw him from the car window. I do not forget his eyes, threatening and at the same time seductive." He described the second encounter, which also took place in Argentina, as 'stronger than the previous one,' writing that the devil looked at him with 'eyes of fire' like rays of fire before he ran away clutching the Rosary and pleading with the Virgin Mary.

The diary describes Pope Francis's reaction to a clerical sexual abuse scandal, with the pontiff saying he saw the 'gates of hell' after realizing how serious the situation was. The book also sheds light on tensions within the Vatican and Roman Curia during his papacy, including decisions he took and others he avoided.

Among issues discussed was the possibility of ordaining married men as priests, a proposal that Fernandez said Francis wanted to pursue but ultimately avoided because of concerns about internal divisions. Fernandez revealed that when they prepared the document allowing blessings for same-sex couples, there was 'a very harsh reaction.' Some of Pope Francis's reforms were subsequently moderated by his successor, Pope Leo XIV, formerly known as Robert Prevost, according to the excerpts.
items.title: Pope Francis' Private Diary Reveals Visions of Devil and Clergy Debates

With Black Friday arriving on November 27 in Australia, a leading market research company predicts shoppers will spend a record $7.2 billion during the four-day period from November 27-30 — an increase of 5.5% over last year and an average per-shopper spend of $920, up $116 from 2025 (figures attributed to the unnamed research company). Australian consumer research from 2025 found that 64% of shoppers consider price discounts important when purchasing, while 89% wait for sales or promotions before buying in at least one category. The article warns that some online retailers use "dark patterns" — deceptive tactics designed to pressure people into purchases they might otherwise avoid — including countdown timers that create false urgency (such as a timer claiming only ten minutes remain), low-stock warnings like messages stating "only two left in stock" or "20 people are viewing this item," and discount labels showing crossed-out prices such as $100 reduced from $200 to imply 50% savings even when the original price was never genuinely applied. The article notes there is no foolproof way for shoppers to verify whether a countdown deadline is genuine beforehand, recommending they compare prices with other retailers, check product needs, and avoid letting timers dictate decisions.

On regulation, in September 2026 the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) announced that retailers Vuly and James Lane had paid $39,600 and $19,800 penalties respectively following allegations of misleading Black Friday promotions. Then on November 10, the ACCC announced another investigation into Black Friday sales advertising to examine potentially misleading countdown timers, discount claims, low-stock warnings and testimonials — with its checks extending for the first time across websites, emails and social media. The watchdog's earlier investigation found concerning advertising claims in about half of the 50 retailers reviewed, noting that under Australian consumer law businesses cannot make false or misleading claims about prices, discounts or promotions.

The article also notes international efforts: the European Union's Digital Services Act aims to restrict deceptive website designs on online platforms, and in the United States the Federal Trade Commission Act prohibits unfair or deceptive business practices. It concludes with practical advice for shoppers — comparing prices using price history tools, questioning countdown timers, reading discount conditions, checking final prices including delivery fees, verifying sellers against unfamiliar websites offering unusually large discounts, and deciding before browsing by making a shopping list and setting a budget — while noting that potentially misleading promotions can be reported to the ACCC.
items.title: Black Friday Spending Forecast as ACCC Investigates Misleading Online Retail Tactics

In a keynote at the AI Engineer Code Summit, delivered around November 24th 2026—the one-year anniversary of Claude Opus 4.5's release—an author identified three significant inflection points in large language model and coding agent capabilities over the past twelve months.

The first occurred in November 2025 with Claude Opus 4.5, which Anthropic described as handling ambiguity and reasoning about tradeoffs without hand-holding; testers reportedly found it could resolve complex multi-system bugs that were near-impossible for Sonnet 4.5 weeks earlier. The author noted the model became reliably correct on daily coding tasks within Claude Code—then nine months old—and cited OpenAI's November release of GPT-5.1 Instant, Thinking, Codex, and Codex-Max as having a similar effect on its Codex agent.

The second inflection point emerged in June/July with "Fable class models," introduced by Claude Mythos (announced April 2026 but deemed too dangerous to release due to improved cybersecurity capabilities) and followed by the export-controlled Claude Fable 5, which was withheld from the author until July 1st. The author defined these as relentlessly proactive systems—citing a June example where Fable autonomously built a screenshot mechanism and logging server—and listed Claude Opus 5.5 ("cheap Fable") and GPT-6 Astra among models reaching this class.

The third inflection point, in September/October, involved frontier LLMs becoming highly capable at 3D modeling via Blender or Three.js code; the author attributed this to Claude Fable 5 initially kicking into gear with Opus 5.5 (released September 22nd), GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and Gemini 4.

The author also weighed whether Fable 5.2 constitutes a fourth inflection point or an incremental improvement, describing it as matching their own taste in software development while noting the indie games scene's culture war over AI-assisted programming.
items.title: Three LLM Inflection Points in Twelve Months

items.summary: The U.S. Army plans a controlled detonation of nearly the entire national stockpile of lead azide on Wednesday morning at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, about 10 miles west across the Mississippi River from Illinois and roughly 160 miles southeast of Des Moines. About 9,700 pounds (nearly 5 tons) of the compound is stored in 68 drums that inspectors discovered had begun to crystallize in March, making it unstable enough that movement or even a shock could trigger a spontaneous explosion. After consulting with the EPA and other agencies, officials decided detonation was the safest option; an emergency permit issued November 16 cleared the way, though Iowa Governor Kim Reynolds, governor-elect Rob Sand, and Earthjustice had urged a delay before a federal appeals court ruled Monday that it could proceed.
items.title: U.S. Army to Detonate Entire National Lead Azide Stockpile in Iowa

items.summary: Last week, mathematician Levent Alpöge announced a proof of the Riemann hypothesis—one of mathematics' most significant outstanding problems—using Claude to generate it while working at Anthropic. The announcement follows several other major mathematical breakthroughs enabled by or completed through large language model-based systems, which has left the field in a state of upset. Details about the proof itself remain limited because mathematicians are still digesting it. The Riemann hypothesis dates from the mid-1800s and was formulated by Bernhard Riemann; while its details cannot be described simply, it carries implications for prime number distribution with significance spanning areas from number theory to cryptography, leading pure mathematicians to consider it one of the most important problems in the field. Alpöge's announcement is written in a somewhat florid style, including an example sentence about 'one of which was already new and shocking,' and he has apparently dropped hints that some parts were meant in jest.
items.title: Mathematician Levent Alpöge Announces AI-Assisted Proof of Riemann Hypothesis

The Reserve Bank of India has proposed the Draft Amendment Directions for 'Preventive Safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs),' which would come into force on July 1, 2027, or earlier at a bank's discretion. Some provisions expanding the definition of bank negligence are set to take effect from January 1, 2027.

Under the proposed rules, customers can switch off digital payment facilities, set transaction limits and temporarily block all outgoing payments through a stop switch facility that immediately disables outward future debits linked to their account. However, this would not cover recurring payment mandates or standing instructions, liens for due charges or loan instalments, bank-initiated recovery debits, inward credits into the account, new UPI registrations on third-party apps, or creation of new payment mandates and standing instructions.

The RBI has also proposed a Trusted Person Mechanism (TPM) as an additional authentication layer. Customers could register a trusted person aged 18 years or above to authenticate certain electronic fund transfers through physical and digital banking channels when the transaction exceeds a customer-set threshold, but not for UPI-linked payments, merchant payments or recurring standing instructions.

Customers may gain greater control over debit card, credit card and prepaid payment instrument transactions by switching on or off different types of transactions and setting or modifying limits within overall issuer-prescribed limits. Banks would also have to provide facilities to set or modify transaction limits for digital payment channels other than cards.

The RBI proposes that banks keep all digital payment channels disabled by default at customer onboarding, enabling them only upon explicit consent with applicable authentication requirements. For debit and credit cards issued by the RBI, physical and virtual cards should be enabled initially only for contact-based usage (ATMs and Point of Sale devices) within India, while forex prepaid cards would be enabled for both contact and contactless use outside India.

For other digital payment channels, banks enabling a channel at onboarding or later must specify an aggregate ceiling on fund transfers over the initial 24 hours, with gradual enhancements allowed afterward based on channel risk assessment and internal policy. The draft also defines bank negligence as any act of omission or commission contributing to fraudulent electronic banking transactions, including failures in authentication instructions, multi-factor authentication for new account linkages, mandatory alerts, fraud reporting channels, prompt action on customer notifications, blocking digital payment channels after failed login attempts, providing customer-induced controls and the Trusted Person Mechanism, system malfunctions or security breaches, and employee collusion.
items.title: RBI Proposes Stricter Rules Against Digital Fraud

E-commerce company Amazon announced Wednesday that it has reached $27 billion in cumulative exports from India through its Amazon Global Selling programme, with the number of exporters on the platform rising 20 per cent over a year to 2.4 lakh (approximately 240,000). The milestone marks progress toward Amazon's goal of enabling $80 billion in cumulative e-commerce exports from India by 2030, according to a company statement.

The programme was launched in 2015 and has enabled the sale of more than one billion 'Made-in-India' products to customers across Amazon's global marketplaces. Among states and Union Territories, Delhi topped the list with over 36,000 exporters, followed by Rajasthan (over 32,500), Uttar Pradesh (over 29,000), Gujarat (over 28,000) and Maharashtra (over 23,500).

items.title: Amazon's e-commerce exports from India reach $27 billion as exporter count rises 20%

items.summary:
The International Energy Agency (IEA) has identified a growing gap between installed solar power capacity and Chinese panel imports across developing countries in Africa, West Asia, and Southeast Asia, which it terms the "missing PV panels" phenomenon. The IEA attributes this discrepancy to increasing reliance on decentralized off-grid solar systems among consumers with limited electricity access or facing daily blackouts of 8-10 hours, noting that such grid-unconnected installations are difficult for governments to track and thus classified as off-grid in its dataset.

The West Asia conflict, which erupted on February 20, 2026, served as a tailwind for the trend. The IEA reported that amid energy market disruptions from the conflict, solar panel imports from China into Africa, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia rose sharply during March to May of this year.

The gap is most pronounced in Pakistan, where official statistics report only around 10 GW of installed solar PV capacity as of March 2026, but imports reached nearly 50 GW from 2020 to 2025. The IEA noted that although Pakistan shows the largest absolute gap compared with Africa and ASEAN, many developing economies with limited electricity access register a discrepancy of over 50 per cent.

The trend is projected to drive significant off-grid solar PV expansion in the IEA's forecast: growth for 2026-2031 is expected to increase 2.5-fold from the 2020-2025 period, with almost 80 GW of off-grid capacity to be installed through 2031. Outside Pakistan, Sub-Saharan Africa is set to lead this surge with more than 21 GW of new installations over 2026-2031—equivalent to the region's total installed capacity today. In ASEAN, about 10 GW of additional off-grid capacity is projected—a tenfold increase from a current capacity of less than 1 GW.

The IEA also noted that these "missing" panels reflect global trade complexities, as some Chinese-imported solar PV panels are re-exported to developing economies to avoid tariffs in other markets.
items.title: IEA Points to Hidden Solar Boom in Developing Regions via 'Missing PV Panels'

Hyundai will be among the first automakers to partner with the service, offering both new and used electric, hybrid, and petrol vehicles including the IONIQ 3, IONIQ 5, KONA, and i20 models.
