At the Vettri Investment and Conversion Conclave held near Chennai on Wednesday (November 25), Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay signed 78 memoranda of understanding on behalf of the Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce Department. The agreements are expected to bring a cumulative investment of Rs 58,214 crore and generate employment for 65,786 persons, according to an official release from the state government.

Alongside these new pacts, Vijay advanced execution of previously committed projects, bringing the day's total industrial outlay to Rs 67,569 crore with a combined employment potential of 87,461 jobs. During the conclave, he laid foundation stones for 15 new industrial projects worth Rs 7,925 crore, which are projected to create 19,965 jobs across the state. He also inaugurated six completed projects valued at Rs 1,430 crore, generating immediate employment opportunities for 1,710 individuals.

In addition to these actions, Vijay distributed appointment orders to 18 candidates selected for various roles across five companies during the event.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Signs 78 MoUs Worth Rs 58,214 Crore at Investment Conclave

items.summary: Police reported that three men were killed and two others seriously injured after the vehicle they were traveling in collided with a trolley late Tuesday night on the Delhi-Jaipur National Highway (NH-48). The incident occurred near the Dahmi flyover in the Behror area, where five young men from Mundanwada village—identified as Harish Kumar, Devendra Prajapat and Hemant Prajapat among the deceased—were returning to their village from Bhagwadi. According to police, around 1 a.m., their vehicle lost control and crashed into the trolley from behind; the collision badly mangled the front of the car and trapped all five occupants inside. The three men died on the spot while the two injured were rushed to a hospital for treatment. Behror station house officer Ravindra said he received information about the accident near the flyover around 1 a.m., found that a car had collided with the trolley from behind, and confirmed the deaths and injuries at the scene. The bodies of the deceased were moved to the mortuary of Behror hospital for post-mortem examination, and police stated an investigation is underway to determine the exact cause of the accident.
items.title: Three Killed When Car Rams Trolley on Delhi-Jaipur Highway

items.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government on Wednesday carried out a major police reshuffle, transferring 28 IPS and Provincial Police Service (PPS) officers. The state reported the move as involving 10 IPS officers from the 2020, 2021, and 2022 batches along with 18 additional SP-rank officers and PAC commandants; a separate figure of two IPS officers posted to Lucknow was also cited in coverage. The reshuffle brought significant changes to the Lucknow police commissionerate, where three new ADCPs were added: IPS Punit Dwivedi (2020 batch) and Mavis Tok (2022 batch), both posted as additional deputy commissioners of police (ADCPs), along with Induprabha Singh, an additional SP-rank PPS officer. Amit Kumawat was shifted from Lucknow to Ghaziabad as ADCP, while Naveen Kumar Singh was posted as staff officer to the director general of police at police headquarters and ADCP Kiran Yadav transferred to the Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) as additional SP (operations). Other commissionerate-level changes included Neetu (2020 batch) moving from Varanasi to Gautam Buddh Nagar, Shaivya Goyal (2021 batch) transferring from Gautam Buddh Nagar to Ghaziabad, and Shiva Singh shifting from Kanpur to Agra as ADCP. At the district level, Pushkar Verma moved from Prayagraj commissionerate to Fatehgarh as additional SP while Aditya transferred from Agra to Budaun as additional SP (rural), Bhavre Diksha Arun shifted from Shahjahanpur to the Police Training School in Meerut as additional SP, Raj Kumar Ranvijay Singh moved from Moradabad to Azamgarh as additional SP (rural), Abhishek Tiwari shifted from Mainpuri to Moradabad as additional SP (city), Anup Kumar transferred from Mau to Sonbhadra, and Piyush Kumar Singh moved from Ghaziabad commissionerate to Mainpuri as additional SP (rural). Mamta Kuril was posted as additional SP (traffic) in Muzaffarnagar after serving as additional SP (crime) in Aligarh. Girish Kumar Singh moves from Fatehgarh to Aligarh as additional SP (crime), while Atul Kumar Chaubey shifted from Muzaffarnagar to Mathura as additional SP (security). Among specialised units, Shrestha was posted as deputy commandant of the 49th PAC battalion in Gautam Buddh Nagar after serving as additional SP in the Anti-Terrorist Squad at Lucknow, and Naveena Shukla transferred from ANTF to the Anti-Corruption Organisation headquarters in Lucknow. The PAC and training establishments were also reorganised: Nitin Kumar Singh was posted as additional SP at PTS Moradabad after being deputy commandant of the 49th PAC battalion; Vibha Singh appointed deputy commandant of the sixth PAC battalion in Meerut from PTS Meerut, while Raghavendra Kumar Mishra transferred to the fifth battalion of the Special Security Force in Saharanpur. Devendra Singh-I shifted from the 39th PAC battalion in Mirzapur to Shahjahanpur as additional SP (rural), Arun Kumar Singh-II moved from the traffic directorate at Lucknow to Azamgarh as additional SP (traffic), Hridesh Katheria transferred from Budaun to the traffic directorate at Lucknow, and Pankaj Kumar Srivastava moved from Azamgarh to Mau as additional SP.
items.title: Uttar Pradesh Carries Out Major Police Reshuffle, Moving 28 Officers

items.summary: Chinese technology companies have increased investment in research and development while accelerating innovation across AI computing power, cloud services, large language models, and commercial applications. Alibaba's financial results show revenue from AI cloud and computing services grew 53% year on year, with external commercialization revenue rising 64%, as AI-related product revenue has recorded triple-digit growth for 13 consecutive quarters. At the Yunqi Conference, Alibaba's chip subsidiary T-Head unveiled its next-generation Zhenwu V900 AI chip, scheduled to go on sale in the first quarter of 2027, alongside a next-generation supernode product powered by the chip. Tencent continues upgrading its Hunyuan large language model with more computing resources allocated to model-as-a-service offerings and GPU leasing; when Hy4 was released in November, it ranked first among Chinese models on the Agent Arena leaderboard for task success rate, user satisfaction, and steerability. WorkBuddy has become China's most widely used AI product by token consumption, with over 10 million users collectively consuming more than 100 trillion tokens daily while its enterprise customer base grows. In Egypt, Chinese companies have covered computing services and training costs for eligible startups to help develop Arabic-language models, lowering barriers to entry for local businesses. The Hill reported that as Chinese AI products gain use across Africa, Asia, and Latin America—supporting infrastructure, classrooms, airports, and government services—localized cloud services are helping expand their presence in the Global South. Tan Poh Hwee, president of the Asia Academy of Digital Economics in Singapore, told Xinhua that China's notable contribution has been moving technologies from laboratories into large-scale production; a model in Singapore's national Sea-Lion series is based on a Chinese AI model so local teams can focus resources on regional languages and industry-specific knowledge. Simon Bridges, CEO of the Auckland Business Chamber in New Zealand, said at the APEC CEO Summit that cooperation remains important amid the current global landscape, citing open-source models as an example of China making technological benefits more accessible across the region.
items.title: Chinese AI Companies Report Strong Growth and Expand Global Reach

items.summary: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government in Tamil Nadu defied a Supreme Court order permitting the one-time lighting of a lamp at a disputed stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill near Madurai on Karthigai Deepam, which was celebrated Tuesday. The Hindu reported that Vijay-led TVK officials told the court Wednesday they could not comply because the Arulmigu Subramania Swamy temple administration refused to authorize lighting at the pillar, citing a violation of traditional rituals; instead, per an affidavit filed by Madurai District Collector Nishant Krishn and reported by Bar and Bench, the ceremonial lamp was lit only at the customary spot near the Uchi Pillaiyar temple atop the hill. Krishn also tendered an apology to the court after recording an undertaking with the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Tuesday to abide by Supreme Court directions. The Supreme Court had allowed the one-time lighting as a measure for Karthigai Deepam, while upholding the Madras High Court order permitting the ritual but staying its other observations concerning the pillar's nature and land ownership. On December 1, High Court judge GR Swaminathan ruled that the stone pillar is a deepathoon designed to hold lamps and ordered the temple to restore lighting there, holding it would not infringe on the nearby Muslim shrine; another bench upheld this order on January 6 but said only temple management members could light the lamp without public accompaniment. The Vijay-led government challenged that High Court order on June 11. The decision to light the lamp solely at the customary Uchi Pillaiyar mandapam triggered protests by Bharatiya Janata Party leaders and Hindu organization members at the foothills, reported The Hindu; several protesters including BJP state chief Nainar Nagenthran were detained before being released, while some demonstrators vandalized buses and public property. Thousands of police personnel were deployed to maintain order ahead of the ceremony as the disputed pillar was barricaded, and Krishn imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita until Wednesday per PTI. BJP leader Narayanan Thirupathy called the government's refusal an "arrogant remark" that would "face consequences," reported The New Indian Express.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Defies Supreme Court Order on Karthigai Deepam Lamp at Disputed Thiruparankundram Pillar

items.summary: Bilateral trade between China and Italy exceeded €60 billion in the first nine months of 2026, with Italian exports to China rising by around 20% year on year, according to Italian Ambassador to China Massimo Ambrosetti. The figures were cited at the 13th Notte Italiana gala held in Beijing on November 21, an event organized by the China-Italy Chamber of Commerce (CICC) that brought together roughly 500 guests, including Chinese and Italian institutional representatives and business leaders.
items.title: China-Italy bilateral trade surpasses €60 billion as Italy promotes economic ties at Beijing gala

items.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo reimposed a ban on cobalt exports effective next week in an effort to raise the price of the metal, for which it holds the world's largest reserves. The restriction sent shares of some Chinese miners soaring, highlighting their dominance over global cobalt production and its role as a key ingredient in the energy transition. According to Kinshasa, the move is part of plans to build strategic reserves of several key minerals to strengthen control over supply amid competition between China and the US for access to Africa's mineral resources; while Washington seeks to loosen Beijing's grip on these chains, Chinese firms continue to dominate many critical-mineral supply networks.
items.title: DRC Reimposes Cobalt Export Ban as Prices Fall

items.summary: Malaysia's state energy company Petronas has forecast that the global liquefied natural gas market will remain relatively tight in 2027, with elevated prices likely to persist until additional supply becomes available. Executive VP and chief executive for gas and maritime business Datuk Adif Zulkifli stated this expectation as quoted by Bernama, attributing continued pressure on LNG markets to ongoing Middle East supply disruptions. The forecast depends on several factors including the duration of conflict in the region and the pace of global LNG supply growth, which has accelerated because importers are seeking alternatives to Qatari and Emirati gas. Qatar has struggled to restore LNG flows while oil exporters have boosted exports through ship-to-ship transfers; although such transfers were reported earlier outside the Strait of Hormuz, they appear less widely adopted by LNG exporters than by oil producers. U.S. LNG exports reached all-time highs this year with a similar trend expected into 2027, and Africa is emerging as another major source, with sub-Saharan African exports projected to rise 175% by 2034 following development of new projects in Mozambique, Nigeria, Senegal, and Mauritania. Separately, Rystad Energy cited El Niño conditions that may bring warmer weather and a milder-than-normal winter across key Northern Hemisphere LNG-consuming regions as factors that could weaken short-term gas demand growth by curbing heating needs and easing price pressure, while persistently high prices might encourage greater reliance on coal-fired power generation in Asia. The report was authored by Irina Slav for Oilprice.com.
items.title: Petronas Forecasts Tight Global LNG Market Through 2027

items.summary: A South African court on Tuesday convicted and sentenced Tafadzwa Sithole, a Zimbabwean man, for attempting to travel to Russia to fight in its war against Ukraine. He was arrested earlier this month along with eight others after entering South Africa legally on November 4 and staying at accommodation in Kempton Park, east of Johannesburg, in preparation for his journey. On November 8, he was arrested at O.R. Tambo International Airport while attempting to board a flight to Russia.
items.title: South African Court Convicts Zimbabwean Man of Attempting to Join Russian War

items.summary: Unknown attackers reportedly breached an open-source intelligence (OSINT) analysis system at the US Central Intelligence Agency, according to a source familiar with the matter who spoke to The New York Times. The cyberattack was carried out using the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework and also affected the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. While the CIA and ODNI have not yet responded to a request for more details, no classified data or systems were exposed in the breach; the source stated that 'the hack did not involve our classified networks or classified information, and no other systems are currently at risk.' Hours after the report, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed it was investigating a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems. After detecting the attack, FinCEN took some systems offline as a precaution and directed banks to use the Financial Institutions Hotline to file reports because some services may be unavailable. BleepingComputer reached out to a FinCEN spokesperson with questions about the incident but did not receive an immediate response.
items.title: Hackers Breach CIA OSINT System Using ARTEX AI Framework

items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition announced Wednesday that its air defenses intercepted and destroyed four drones over Ras Tanura in the kingdom's Eastern Province, according to a statement posted on X by coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki. Maliki said several fragments fell during the operation and an initial assessment found no injuries. The interceptions followed a drone attack one day earlier that targeted a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District, injuring 11 people per Saudi Civil Defense; Maliki blamed Yemen's Houthi group for both incidents amid escalating hostilities between the Houthis and coalition forces.
items.title: Saudi-led Coalition Intercepts Drones Over Eastern Province as Regional Tensions Escalate

items.summary:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has reinstated Senegal as the winner of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations, overturning an earlier decision that had awarded the trophy to Morocco after Senegalese players walked off the pitch during the final. The ruling came after returning to the field, Senegal won the match 1-0 in extra time; a prior appeals panel had instead ruled a 3-0 default victory for Morocco.

Morocco's Football Federation has vowed to pursue "all necessary legal avenues" and said it could take the case to Switzerland's Federal Supreme Court. The federation objected to what it called "contact" between one of the CAS panel members and the head of the Senegalese football federation days before the decision was announced.

Moroccan fans reacted with disappointment, though responses varied. Jad Ouchtaqalla said he had hoped the tournament would stay in Morocco because his country deserved it and expressed shock at the decision. Amine Saadi accepted the outcome but noted they would have liked to keep the trophy there and hope to win a future edition. Fan Rachid Debbi, by contrast, was not surprised by the ruling, saying he had expected Senegal to be awarded the trophy since they initially took it.

items.title: Morocco to challenge CAS ruling reinstating Senegal as AFCON champions

items.summary:
Domestic energy prices are set to rise in January under Ofgem's new price cap, affecting millions of households across England, Scotland and Wales. The BBC spoke with three people about how they're reducing their gas and electricity costs.

Kelly Anne Harvey, a 44-year-old building surveyor from Cleveleys near Blackpool with a combined household income of £60,000, currently pays about £154 a month for gas and electricity on a standard variable rate with Octopus. She's seeking a fixed-rate deal to offset the rise after her family fell into arrears previously. To manage costs she pays by direct debit—typically £138 cheaper annually than paying when bills arrive—and uses electric blankets and portable oil radiators so central heating runs less often. Her household participates in Octopus's energy-saving scheme, which rewards reduced peak-time use with a free weekend hour; on Sundays they run the dishwasher, tumble drier, washing machine, and may charge their electric cars.

Stacey, 40, a single mother from Bristol on a fixed-term tracker tariff with E.On Next (rates below the quarterly Ofgem cap), expects to pay £1,800 for energy this year—up £400 on last year. She's turned her central heating down from 22C to 19.5C, bought electric blankets, and pays by direct debit. She also keeps curtains shut to retain heat, has her daughters wear thermal clothing when cold, and uses less hot water.

Around 1.5 million UK households rely on heating oil for heating and hot water, with costs already rising over the past year due to global oil market disruption. Bradley Knowles, 32, a finance worker in rural Lincolnshire living with his husband, mother and sister, noted that when he moved two years ago a litre of heating oil cost 50-60p; at the height of the Iran war it reached £1.20 or £1.30, now stabilising around £1. He orders oil in bulk—1,000 to 1,500 litres (the candidate readings list "500" as an alternative figure)—preferably in summer when prices are lower and a few weeks ahead to avoid costly next-day delivery.

Bradley uses comparison sites for the cheapest local suppliers, sets aside money monthly so he can always afford orders, and avoids leaving oil-powered boilers on all day. Instead he uses an electric tank to store warm water and tops up heating in parts of the property with electric radiators.
items.title: BBC Profiles Three UK Households Cutting Energy Costs Amid January Price-Cap Rise

items.summary: Goldman Sachs has forecast that the proliferation of data centers will drive demand for natural gas in the United States over the next two years, estimating that some 52 GW of new data center capacity could be added to the grid in 2028 alone. In a note cited by Reuters this week, the bank's analysts wrote that year-to-date, data-center power capacity and demand have increased by nearly 30% in the US, contributing to more than one third of total U.S. power demand growth. The analysts said they expect growth acceleration in data centers to be driven not only by a higher volume of facilities but also by increasingly larger physical footprints and higher power density.
items.title: Goldman Sachs Forecasts U.S. Natural Gas Demand Surge from Data Center Boom

items.summary: Jasveer Singh, CEO of Gurugram-based KnotDating, shared on X a marriage requirement he described as something he had never heard before: an IIT graduate earning Rs 1.27 crore wants a wife who grew up in a small town, moved to a big city, and became successful like him. Raised in a tiny town where he attended school through Class 12, Singh relocated to a large metropolis, enrolled at IIT, and built a prosperous career. He said it was difficult to find a spouse because the women who matched well on paper came from affluent families in South Bombay and South Delhi; their upbringing, lifestyle, tastes, and views on family and relationships differed sharply from his. Singh explained that these wealthy metro women understood his present but not his past, while women who had never left small towns understood his past but not his present. He then met women from small towns, but he said their interests did not match after a decade in metro cities, leaving him feeling stuck between two worlds. His stated requirement is for an educated, independent and successful woman who has experienced both worlds, because such women connect with him instantly since they understand both his past and present. Singh referred to this as his 'Two-Nation Theory'—two completely different worlds within the same country—and claimed he was seeking a similar life path rather than a job or family money.
items.title: IIT Graduate Earning Rs 1.27 Crore Seeks Wife Who Shared His Small-Town-to-Metro Journey
